subject: Clarifying PO line items and mapping per-token tiers to preferred-vendor form
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@greenfield.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: vendorforms@greenfield.health, Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@greenfield.health>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request — preferred vendor form + PO format for Hosted API pricing

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — procurement is reviewing the Hosted API pricing you shared. A couple of things came up while we digest the model:

- Our standard preferred-vendor form (attached) requires a discrete unit and unit price on the PO line. We can’t accept a PO that references an external rate card for core pricing.
- Your pricing is usage-based (per-token) with volume tiers. Procurement needs guidance on how to represent that on a single PO line so finance can process it.
- Also please provide Redwood’s legal name, tax ID / W-9, and bank remit for ACH.

Can you send a template PO line item (example quantity + unit price) and note how you recommend handling true-up/reconciliation for token usage at month/quarter end? We have an internal deadline to return a signed vendor form by 2027-03-09.

Attached: preferred_vendor_form_GFH.pdf

Best,
Anika Shah
Sr. Procurement Manager
Greenfield Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@greenfield.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — preferred vendor form + PO format for Hosted API pricing

Hi Anika —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attached form. We can absolutely work with your procurement team — we just want to keep the billing mechanics transparent. High-level proposal:

1) Template PO line (example):
   - Item: Hosted API — Committed Tokens (March 2027)
   - Unit: Token (estimated)
   - Quantity: 1,000,000 (example estimate for the month)
   - Unit price: $0.0009 per token (blended per-token price at Tier 2 commit)
   - Extended price: $900.00

2) Reconciliation: invoices will initially bill to the committed/estimated quantity. At the end of the invoice period (monthly, or quarterly if you prefer), we reconcile actual usage against committed quantity and issue a credit or additional invoice for the delta. We can include a short exhibit in the vendor form that describes the reconciliation window and invoicing cadence.

3) Contract language workaround: if the preferred-vendor form must show a single line item and not reference another doc, we can populate the line with an "Estimated Committed Tokens" quantity and include a required exhibit (Exhibit A: Rate Card & Reconciliation) as an appendix to the vendor form. Exhibit A will be the authoritative rate schedule.

4) Docs we can provide now: Redwood legal name, tax ID, W-9; a sample PO line we use in enterprise deals; and our standard reconciliation language. Attached: redwood_ratecard_q1_2027.pdf and a sample PO line for your review.

If that approach works for procurement, send back the vendor form with the fields you prefer us to fill and we’ll return it with Exhibit A attached.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call with your procurement rep tomorrow if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_ratecard_q1_2027.pdf, sample_PO_line.txt

From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@greenfield.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: vendorforms@greenfield.health, Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@greenfield.health>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — preferred vendor form + PO format for Hosted API pricing

Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick reply and the sample attachments. Procurement reviewed the reconciliation approach and we have two constraints:

1) Our AP system requires a unit column and cannot reference an external exhibit for core pricing. The PO lines must show a unit and unit price that match what we intend to pay.
2) Legal would prefer minimal external references on the face of the PO to keep contracts machine-readable for our systems.

We can accept your reconciliation proposal if Redwood provides an initial PO line as a single "blended" unit price for the estimated quantity, and you commit in a signed annex to reconcile usage monthly and issue invoice adjustments accordingly. Please also provide:

- Legal entity name to appear on the PO (exact)
- Tax ID / W-9
- Wire/ACH remit instructions

I attached the vendor form with a few redlines showing the fields procurement needs filled (see vendor_form_filled_redlines.pdf). If you can return the filled form with the blended PO line and the annex language included, we can process to signature.

Attached: vendor_form_filled_redlines.pdf

Regards,
Anika

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@greenfield.health>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — preferred vendor form + PO format for Hosted API pricing

Anika — thanks for the redlines. Sharing a simple template we use for clients who require a single-line PO:

PO Line (example):
- Description: Redwood Inference — Hosted API (Committed Tokens month X)
- Unit: Committed token unit (blended)
- Quantity: 1,000,000 (estimated monthly tokens)
- Unit Price: $0.00095 (blended rate reflecting Tier 2 discount)
- Extended Price: $950.00

Reconciliation mechanics (we will include as Annex A):
- At the end of the invoice period we compare actual token usage to the committed quantity. If actual > committed, Redwood invoices the overage at the agreed per-token overage rate. If actual < committed, Redwood credits the difference to the next invoice. Credits are applied within one billing cycle.
- For bookkeeping we can issue a monthly invoice against the PO, and a quarterly reconciliation statement.

Attached is a PO_template.xlsx you can drop into your AP system. We will also include: Redwood legal name = "Redwood Inference, Inc.", Tax ID = 12-3456789 (W-9 attached), ACH remit: Redwood Inference, Inc. / Bank: First Redwood Bank / Routing: 012345678 / Account: 987654321.

If those details are acceptable, Evelyn or I will fill the vendor form and return it with Annex A and the rate card bound into the PDF. For transparency: invoice-level reconciliation is standard for usage-based products and it has worked for other enterprise finance teams.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: PO_template.xlsx

Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — preferred vendor form + PO format for Hosted API pricing

Team —

Finance is okay with the blended PO + monthly reconciliation approach for this deal (deal id GFH-2027-137) provided we:

- Cap retrospective exposures to one invoice period (monthly) and perform reconciliation monthly.
- Include clear phrasing in Annex A about how overages/credits are calculated and timing for credits to appear.
- Approve net45 as standard; we can accept net15 @ 3% early-pay if the customer signs the early-pay election.
- Add a short liability cap and SLA credit reference (CS to handle SLA wording).

Ben/Marissa: please produce the final populated vendor form, include Annex A (Rate Card + Reconciliation), and send to Anika with the W-9 and remit instructions. I will review the final language before signature.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference
